label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
To: Shared/Ops & HR
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT (for Achieng to read before she sleeps) - Sunday brief for Brian: casuals' pay, Embakasi, Monday 30 Nov

CASAUALS' PAY - WHAT BRIAN NEEDS ON MONDAY MORNING
Brief for Brian Ochieng. Read on Sunday. Everything below is confirmed as at 9:40pm tonight, Saturday. Keep this note to yourself, do not circulate it, and do not read parts of it out to the guys.

1. WHAT REALLY HAPPENED WITH FRIDAY'S PAY
- Friday's pay was due on Friday. It did not go out. Nothing to do with the casuals: nobody's work, conduct, numbers or attendance caused this.
- What happened: our bulk bank transfer file failed a technical validation check at the bank (a beneficiary reference field longer than the bank now allows, after their 25 November platform upgrade). The file was rejected and no payments were processed. The rejection alert went to an old finance mailbox that nobody was watching, so it was not seen until after 5pm, after the bank cut-off had passed.
- Where it stands: the whole lot has been switched to M-Pesa bulk (B2C), approved by the MD. Money goes straight to each worker's phone.
- The batch: 212 records, KES 1,846,300. Peninah has confirmed 198 numbers. 14 could not be reached, mostly the new loaders from the Athi River intake.
- If you are asked "why", keep it short: we had a processing error on our side, it is fixed, here is the new date and time. Do not walk them through bank templates and mailbox mix-ups. It reads as an excuse. Apologise, commit, and move on.

2. WHEN THE MONEY LANDS
- Monday by 11am, on the phone, via M-Pesa, to all 198 confirmed numbers. This is Kevin's confirmed position: 11am is what we can commit to. Not earlier.
- Say "11am" as one time, one number. No "around midday", no "should be there by lunch". After Mombasa 2024 we only give times we can keep. That was our rule then and it stays our rule now.
- In the same batch: KES 500 per head for Monday lunch plus fare for every casual on the affected list. M-Pesa charges are on us, so nobody's amount is reduced.
- The 14 unconfirmed numbers: Peninah will be at the depot from 7:30 with the list and a printout and will correct them face to face. She has the laptop for payslips as well. For those 14, do not put a date on the money in the floor - say we will get their number this morning, they will get their lunch money in hand today, and we will confirm the Friday balance in person. Honesty here buys you more than a guess.

3. WHAT BRIAN CAN PROMISE
- Your money is on your phone by 11am Monday. Signed off, batch prepared, scheduled.
- KES 500 lunch money and fare, in the same batch, with no M-Pesa charge deducted from anyone.
- An apology from management, in person, this morning, from Brian, because Achieng is travelling.
- Peninah on site from 7:30 with the list, a printout and the laptop: individual figures on the payslip, corrected on the spot.
- Nobody is being fined, docked, dismissed or threatened over the delay, and no one's contract is at issue today.
- The 14 whose numbers we could not reach will be fixed on site this morning, in person.

4. WHAT BRIAN MUST NOT SAY OR DO
- Must not promise any time earlier than 11am, and must not soften it ("should be", "hopefully", "by lunch"). One time only.
- Must not discuss the company's finances, cash position, funding, overdraft or any customer or creditor. If someone asks "does the company have money?", the answer is: "I am not going to discuss the company's finances. What I can tell you is your money is scheduled for 11am, and I will be standing here when it lands." Route it to Achieng or Kevin.
- Must not name Kevin, the MD or the bank failure as excuses, and must not shift blame to Finance or to the bank in front of the men. Brian apologises, as management, without an excuse.
- Must not threaten anyone with contracts, dismissal or losing their job. Not on Monday, and this is not being soft - it is the written procedure (Casual workers' pay and grievance procedure v3, 3 October): work stoppages are handled by Operations and HR together, and nobody is to be dismissed or threatened with dismissal on the day.
- Must not lecture the men about loyalty, discipline or sacrifice, and must not say "calm down". Acknowledge, commit, move.
- Must not quote individual pay figures from memory. Point people to Peninah and the payslip.
- Must not pay out cash to the 198 - everything goes by M-Pesa so there is a record. Cash only for the 14 we could not reach, given in person by Peninah and logged.
- Must not announce a new deadline or change the payment route on the floor.

5. IF OUMA'S GROUP WILL NOT LOAD THE KISUMU TRUCKS
Joseph says Monday 6am will be hot and that Ouma and two others are telling people not to load until they see money. The Kisumu trucks must be loaded and out by 9am to hold the offloading slot at the mill, so the pressure is real and it is on us, not on them.

Step 1, before anything else: talk to Ouma alone, privately, away from the group and out of earshot of the loading bay, before addressing everyone. He is loud and he will speak for the others when they can hear him, but he is not a bad man - four kids, rent due. Take him as a man with responsibilities, not as a ringleader. Never call him a troublemaker where others can hear.

Step 2: ask, do not tell. "Tell me what you need to see this morning." Listen first. Then offer only what we actually have: money in his phone by 11am, his KES 500 and fare, an apology in person, his payslip from Peninah, and the 14 numbers being fixed on site. Ask him to hold his people and help get the trucks out by 9. Give him a reason and a date, not a threat.

Step 3: then address the whole group once, in one short conversation.

Step 4: if loading still stops - no threats, no arguments in front of the group, no dismissal talk. Write it down: time, who was present, who said what, which trucks, what is physically blocked. WhatsApp Achieng before she boards (she is up from 4:30, boarding 7:05, JKIA T1A) and call if it is live; if she cannot be reached, Kevin. Any grievance goes to Joseph first, then to HR within 48 hours, and any stoppage is handled by Operations and HR together, so the wording and the escalation route have to be followed, not improvised.

Step 5: if the trucks cannot leave by 9, that decision is not made on the floor. Call Achieng or Kevin so management can deal with the mill slot.

6. SCRIPT FOR THE GROUP
Brian's words, roughly this, no more than two minutes:

"Morning. I am Brian, operations. Before we start, I am sorry. Friday's pay did not go out. That was our failure, not yours. You worked, you loaded, you did your part. Nothing you did caused this and nobody is being punished for it.

Here is what is happening. Your money is going to your M-Pesa by 11am this morning, the full amount, with no charges taken off. On top of that, everyone on this list gets KES 500 for lunch and your fare, in the same batch. Peninah is here from 7:30 with your payslips - if your number or your figure is wrong, come and see her and we will sort it there.

I know we have given you a time before that we could not keep, and I am not going to stand here and give you a vague promise this morning. It is 11am. The batch is done and scheduled. And I will be standing here when it lands. If anything changes, you will hear it from me first.

If you have a grievance, go to Joseph first and we will take it from there. Nobody is losing their job over this morning. Now let us get the Kisumu trucks loaded and out by 9."

7. IF 11AM SLIPS
- Tell them yourself, in the yard, before they discover a phone that did not buzz. Say what you know and what the new time is.
- WhatsApp Achieng immediately, before 7am if possible. She would rather get the message and act than hear about it later.
- Chase the exceptions first: the 14 unreachable numbers, anyone whose M-Pesa failed, anyone with a transaction error. Check the batch status and the reversals.
- Keep a list of names and numbers of every failed payment and send it to Achieng.

8. WHO IS ON THE GROUND
- Joseph Kiprono, shift supervisor: first point of contact for grievances, already talking to the men since yesterday. Work through him.
- Peninah Auma, payroll: on site 7:30, list, printout, laptop for payslips, correcting the 14 numbers, paying their lunch money where needed.
- Ouma and two others: Ouma first, privately.
- Achieng: WhatsApp until boarding, back Wednesday evening. Brian to WhatsApp her before she boards if anything changes.

9. ASKS BEFORE SHE SLEEPS
- Confirm receipt once Brian has read this, and any change to the plan by 6:30am.
- A decision on whether to ask management to hold the mill slot for a late load - needed before 6am, not after 9.

10. THE FOUR RULES FOR THE DAY
One time only: 11am. Apologise, do not explain. Ouma first, privately. No threats on the day, and nothing about the company's finances.

STATUS: DRAFT. Achieng to read and sign off before Monday. Not for circulation until then.
